tagline: Poland's winter capital sits at the foot of the Tatra Mountains, known for highlander culture, wooden villas, ski slopes and hikes to Morskie Oko lake.
overview: Zakopane is a mountain town in southern Poland, right below the highest peaks of the Tatras on the Slovak border. It became a fashionable resort in the late 1800s, when artists and writers came for the clean air and the culture of the Górale, the local highlanders.

The town gave its name to the Zakopane style, wooden architecture with steep roofs and carved details, seen in villas and churches such as the Chapel in Jaszczurówka. Krupówki Street is the busy main strip, and stalls sell oscypek, smoked sheep's cheese, often grilled with cranberry jam.

In winter Kasprowy Wierch and other slopes offer skiing, and in summer Tatra National Park's trails lead to lakes and peaks, including Morskie Oko, the most famous mountain lake in Poland. The Gubałówka funicular climbs a ridge with views of the whole range.
